Variables.SerializableInputParameter.Name: EnableAccessibilityFeatures
Variables.SerializableInputParameter.Description:
When true the following Accessibility Features are enabled: - Focus States - Skip To Content - Accessible Links - Enhanced Contrasts
These features are implemented in CSS using the "has-accessible-features" Selector

Variables.SerializableInputParameter.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.SerializableInputParameter.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.
Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/ResourcesPage

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebFlow.Name: Advanced2
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebFlow.Description: Flow with all available chart advanced blocks of OutSystems Charts.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: HighchartsModules
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: Extends charts by adding additional Highcharts scripts to the page. Drag-and-drop to a screen to add additional scripts to it. This element will not appear in runtime.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ModulesList
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: List of modules that will be added. By default, the OutSystems Charts has the following modules: accessibility.js, highcharts.js, highcharts-more.js, highcharts-3d.js and no-data-to-display.js.

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: LoadError
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered when the an error(s) occurs during the loading of HighCharts modules into the OutSystems application. T his event provides essential information about the encountered error(s), enabling developers to take appropriate actions to handle these errors gracefully. It's important to note that if multiple modules are being loaded and one of them fails, the LoadError event will be triggered. However, the remaining modules were successfully loaded and the changes are reflected in the charts.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: MessageList
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Each string within the array represents an error message associated with a specific module that failed to load. These messages provide details about the specific issues that occurred, such as the non-existence of a module.

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: Loaded
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered when the High Charts modules are successfully loaded into the application. It is important to note that if a module that has already been loaded is not added again, and will not have any effect and but will trigger this event.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: AddedNewModules
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: When set to true, it indicates that at least one module that was not previously present on the page has been added during the loading process. This parameter serves as an indicator to highlight the addition of new modules.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebFlow.Name: Styles
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebFlow.Description: Flow with all available chart blocks for styling purposes on OutSystems Charts.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebFlow.Name: Charts
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebFlow.Description: Flow with all available chart blocks of OutSystems Charts.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: BarChart
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: The bar chart is a two-dimensional chart where rectangular bars are placed along the x axis with bar length representing the value for a specific category. To customize the elements of the chart (X axis, Y axis, Series Legend, Series, or Tooltip) drag-and-drop the addons into the ChartAddons placeholder inside the Chart block. Note: the addons SS preview won't be visible in runtime.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: DataPointList
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Data that will be used in the chart.Create an aggregate with your data and use it in this field to populate the chart.
Structure: - Value (Decimal) Mandatory - The value to be plotted. - Label (Text) Mandatory - The label of the data point. - SeriesName (Text) - The name of the series where the data point belongs. - Color (Text) - The color of the data point. By default, the chart will be presented with the OutSystems data visualization color palette. To define a custom color for a series, use the Color property of the ChartSeriesStyling block. - Tooltip (Text) - The text that will be displayed on the tooltip of the data point.By default, the tooltip contains the label and value of the point, following the structure [Label]: [Value]. Example: "Apples: 58"

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Height
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the vertical size, in px or %, of the chart. By default, the vertical size is 300px.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: StackingType
ValuesType
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set how the chart labels are handled to be displayed on the chart. The type of the values can be: - Integer: the labels will be displayed as integer numbers. - Decimal: the labels will be displayed as decimal numbers. - Datetime: the labels will be displayed as datetimes. - Text: the labels will be displayed as text and treated as categories. By default, the type is Text.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set additional parameters to customize the bar chart behavior and functionality.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

NRWebWidgets.ReferenceText.Value: To customize your chart, drag addons (ChartXAxis, ChartYAxis, ChartSeriesStyling,..) to this section. This section will not be displayed in runtime.

NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Name: AddOns_Placeholder
NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Description: To customize your chart, drag addons (ChartXAxis, ChartYAxis, ChartSeriesStyling,..) to this section. This section will not be displayed in runtime.

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered when the chart’s data is clicked. It returns information about the chart and data point that was clicked.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: DataPoint

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: DonutChart
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
The donut chart is a circular graph that displays data in rings, where each ring represents a category and the size of the ring corresponds to the value of the data being presented.
The ChartXAxis and ChartYAxis addons are not compatible with this type of chart.
To customize the elements of the chart (Series Legend, Series, or Tooltip) drag-and-drop the addons into the ChartAddons placeholder inside the Chart block. Note: the addons SS preview won't be visible in runtime.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: DataPointList
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Data that will be used in the chart. Create an aggregate with your data and use it in this field to populate the chart.
Structure: - Value (Decimal) Mandatory - The value to be plotted. - Label (Text) Mandatory - The label of the data point. - SeriesName (Text) - The name of the series where the data point belongs. - Color (Text) - The color of the data point. By default, the chart will be presented with the OutSystems data visualization color palette. To define a custom color for a series, use the Color property of the ChartSeriesStyling block. - Tooltip (Text) - The text that will be displayed on the tooltip of the data point. By default, the tooltip contains the label and value of the point, following the structure [Label]: [Value]. Example: "Apples: 58"

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Height
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the vertical size, in px or %, of the chart. By default, the vertical size is 300px.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: InnerSize
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the size, in px or %, of the inner diameter of the Donut chart. If the InnerSize equals to 0, the Donut chart will transform into a Pie chart. By default, the inner size is 50p%.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set additional parameters to customize the donut chart behavior and functionality.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: PieChart
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
The pie chart is a circular graph that displays data in sections, where each section represents a category and the size of the section corresponds to the value of the data being presented.
The ChartXAxis and ChartYAxis addons are not compatible with this type of chart.
To customize the elements of the chart (Series Legend, Series, or Tooltip) drag-and-drop the addons into the ChartAddons placeholder inside the Chart block. Note: the addons SS preview won't be visible in runtime.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: DataPointList
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Data that will be used in the chart. Create an aggregate with your data and use it in this field to populate the chart.
Structure: - Value (Decimal) Mandatory - The value to be plotted. - Label (Text) Mandatory - The label of the data point. - SeriesName (Text) - The name of the series where the data point belongs. - Color (Text) - The color of the data point. By default, the chart will be presented with the OutSystems data visualization color palette. To define a custom color for a series, use the Color property of the ChartSeriesStyling block. - Tooltip (Text) - The text that will be displayed on the tooltip of the data point. By default, the tooltip contains the label and value of the point, following the structure [Label]: [Value]. Example: "Apples: 58"

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Height
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the vertical size, in px or %, of the chart. By default, the vertical size is 300px.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set additional parameters to customize the pie chart behavior and functionality.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

NRWebWidgets.ReferenceText.Value: To customize your chart, drag addons (ChartXAxis, ChartYAxis, ChartSeriesStyling,..) to this section. This section will not be displayed in runtime.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: XAxisFormat
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Formatting options for the X-axis using Highcharts JSON. Action XAxisFormat_Init helps to create and initialize this parameter.
To be compliant with Content Security Policy (CSP) requirements, the support for the eval() function will be discontinued. Consequently, this parameter will be impacted and may not function as expected. It's important to note that this change will only affect those who need to ensure compliance with CSP guidelines.
Additionally, for these non-deprecated parameters, as an alternative we recommend the use of Charts v2.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: YAxisFormat
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Formatting options for the Y-axis using Highcharts JSON. Action YAxisFormat_Init helps to create and initialize this parameter.
To be compliant with Content Security Policy (CSP) requirements, the support for the eval() function will be discontinued. Consequently, this parameter will be impacted and may not function as expected. It's important to note that this change will only affect those who need to ensure compliance with CSP guidelines.
Additionally, for these non-deprecated parameters, as an alternative we recommend the use of Charts v2.

Additionally, for these non-deprecated parameters, as an alternative we recommend the use of Charts v2.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Clickable
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to allow clicking on plotted values and execute the On Click action (False by default).

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: AdvancedFormat
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Information to format chart elements using Highcharts JSON.
To be compliant with Content Security Policy (CSP) requirements, the support for the eval() function will be discontinued. NewRuntime.ReferenceWebFlow.Name: Addons
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebFlow.Description: Flow with all available chart addons of OutSystems Charts.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: ChartYAxis
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: Chart addon used to customize the vertical axis of the chart, though if the chart is inverted this is the horizontal axis (e.g. Bar Chart). Drag-and-drop to the chart Addons placeholder to customize the y axis. When removed from the Addons placeholder, the y axis element will not appear in runtime. Note: This block can't be used for the Pie and Donut charts.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Title
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: The axis title, showing next to the axis line. By default, the axis does not have a title.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Visible
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to display the Y axis and its elements on the chart. False, otherwise. By default, the Y axis is visible.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: MinValue
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: The minimum value of the axis. By default, the MinValue is automatically calculated.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: MaxValue
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: The maximum value of the axis. By default, the MaxValue is automatically calculated.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Label
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Customize the labels that show the data for each tick on the Y axis.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Styling
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Define the styles for the Y axis of the chart.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: GridLines
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Define the styles for the horizontal lines of the chart.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set additional parameters to customize the YAxis behavior and functionality.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: ChartXAxis
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: Chart addon used to customize the horizontal axis of the chart, though if the chart is inverted this is the vertical axis (e.g. Bar Chart). Drag-and-drop to the chart Addons placeholder to customize the x axis. When removed from the Addons placeholder, the x axis element will not appear in runtime. Note: This block can't be used for the Pie and Donut charts.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Title
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: The axis title, showing next to the axis line. By default, the axis does not have a title.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Visible
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to display the X axis and its elements on the chart. False, otherwise. By default, the X axis is visible.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: MinValue

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: MaxValue

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Label

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Styling

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: GridLines

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: ChartLegend
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: Chart addon used to customize the box containing a symbol and a name for each series or data point in the chart. Drag-and-drop to the chart Addons placeholder to customize the series legend. When removed from the Addons placeholder, the legend element will not appear in runtime.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Visible
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to display the legend on the chart. False, otherwise. By default, the chart legend is visible.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Position
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the Legend's position (Default: Bottom). The predefined options are: -Bottom -BottomLeft -BottomRight -Center -Left -Right -Top -TopLeft -TopRight
Examples: - Entities.Position.Right - The Legend is displayed to the right of the chart. - Entities.Position.Bottom - The Legend is displayed underneath the chart.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Layout
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the layout of the legend items. The layout of the legend can be: - Horizontal - Vertical - Proximate: the legend items will be placed as close as possible to the graphs they're representing, except in inverted charts or when the legend position doesn't allow it. Since the Position is calculated based on the charts series, the legend with this layout can only be placed in three positions (center, left, right).
By default, the legend layout is horizontal.
Note: updates to the parameter value after the chart has been draw will not be reflected in runtime.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Styling
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Define the styles for the legend of the chart.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set additional parameters to customize the chart series legend behavior and functionality.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.
Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: ChartExport
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: Chart addon used to add the exporting functionality to the chart. It allows users to: View the chart in full screen, print, download as png, jpeg, pdf,svg, csv and xls. Drag-and-drop to the chart Addons placeholder to add exporting options to the chart.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: FileName
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: The name of the exported file without extension. By default, the file name is "chart".

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: MenuOptions
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to display this option on the exporting menu. Set to False to hide it. By default, True.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Define the optional styles for chart export.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.
Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: ChartSeriesStyling
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: Chart addon used to customize the styling of the chart series. You can bind it to a specific series (by setting the SeriesName) or apply the styles to all of them (by leaving the SeriesName empty). Drag-and-drop to the chart Addons placeholder to customize the series styling. When removed from the Addons placeholder, the styling customizations will be removed.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: SeriesName
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the name of the series to be displayed from your data. The name should match one of the series from the DataPointList.SeriesName. Example: If you have three series: "Installation", "Manufactoring", "Sales & Distribuition", to customize the series "Installation", set the parameter as "Installation".

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: SeriesType
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the type of series, (e.g. line or column). By default, the series type is inherited from chart. Use this property when the chart is a combination of series types. Otherwise, there is no need to set it on the series level.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Marker
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Customize the visual appearance of the data point markers. Markers are the symbols used to represent the data points.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ShowDataPointValues
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to see markers on the chart points. By default, the markers are hidden when the data is dense, and shown for more widespread data points.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Styling
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Define the styles for a given series of the chart.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Define the optional styles for chart series.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

ReferenceClientAction.Name: UpdateChartColorScheme
ReferenceClientAction.Description: A list of color values to use for the chart. Some of the formats accepted are: html, rgb, rgba and hex.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: ChartId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the chart to change the color scheme for.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: ColorScheme
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: A list of color values to use for the chart.

Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Name: Success
Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Description: Boolean that indicates if the action was successfully performed.

Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Name: ErrorMessage
Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Description: Shows details about errors that occur after performing the action. It contains a code and a message explaining the error.

ReferenceClientAction.Name: SetHighchartsSeriesConfigs
ReferenceClientAction.Description: Extend the properties of a series of a chart with additional Highcharts configurations. Due to security reasons, configurations/properties using callback functions cannot be used. Check all Highharts chart properties at: https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/series

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: WidgetId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the chart block.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: SerieName
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The name of the series to be customized. The name should match one of the series from the DataPointList.SeriesName.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: PropertyValueList
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Structure used for charts extensibility with the property path and its value. Example: To remove the series animation , expand the list and add an entry where Property = “animation” and Value = “False”. Check all Highcharts chart properties at: https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/series

Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Name: Success
Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Description: Boolean that indicates if the action was successfully performed.

Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Name: ErrorMessage
Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Description: Shows details about errors that occur after performing the action. It contains a code and a message explaining the error.

Due to security reasons, configurations/properties using callback functions cannot be used. Check all Highharts chart properties at: https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/xAxis

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: WidgetId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the X axis block.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: PropertyValueList
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: List of Highcharts properties and corresponding values. Example: To change the angle of the axis labels, expand the list and add an entry where Property = “angle” and Value = “45”. Check all Highharts chart properties at: https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/xAxis

ReferenceStructureAttribute.Description: The type of axis. The type of the values can be: - Linear: the numbers along the axis are of linear scale. The Chart block ValuesType must be Integer or Decimal. - Logarithmic: the numbers along the axis increase logarithmically and the axis adjusts itself to the data series present in the chart. The Chart block ValuesType must be Integer or Decimal. - Datetime: The Chart block ValuesType must be DateTime. - Category: the names of the categories are used instead of numbers or dates on the axis. The Chart block ValuesType must be Text. By default, the type is linear.

ReferenceAction.Name: AbortTransaction
ReferenceAction.Description: Issues a database ROLLBACK command that undoes all changes performed on the database since the last commit.

ReferenceAction.Name: Logout
ReferenceAction.Description: Logs out a specific user from the application. The 'UserId' and 'Username' session variables are cleared.

ReferenceAction.Name: ListAll
ReferenceAction.Description: Determines if all the elements in the list satisfy the given condition.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: List
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The list that contains the elements to which to apply the condition.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: Condition
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The boolean expression to check for on each element of the list.

Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Name: Result
Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Description: True if every element of the List satisfies the condition; otherwise, False.

ReferenceAction.Name: LogMessage
ReferenceAction.Description: Registers information that can be presented in Service Center in the module general log.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: Message
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The message to add to the module general log.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: ModuleName
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The name of the module to be associated with the log message.

ReferenceAction.Name: ListIndexOf
ReferenceAction.Description: Returns the position of the first element of the List parameter that satisfies the given condition, or -1 if no element satisfying the condition was found.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: List
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The list that contains the elements to which to apply the condition.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: Condition
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The boolean expression to check for on each element of the list.

Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Name: Position
Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Description: The position of the first element of the list that satisfies the given condition; -1 if no element satisfying the condition was found.

ReferenceAction.Name: ListSort
ReferenceAction.Description: Sorts the elements of the List parameter by the given criteria.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: List
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The list that contains the elements to sort by the given criteria.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: By
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The criteria by which to order the elements of the list.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: Ascending
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The boolean expression to indicate if the elements are sorted ascending(True) or descending(False) according to the By parameter. The default value is ascending(True).

ReferenceAction.Name: ListRemove
ReferenceAction.Description: Removes an element from a specific position of a list.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: List
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The list that the element is removed from.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: Position
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Position of the element to be removed.

ReferenceAction.Name: ListFilter
ReferenceAction.Description: Returns a new list with the elements from the List parameter satisfying the given condition.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: SourceList
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The list that contains the elements to which to apply the condition.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: Condition
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The boolean expression to check for on each element of the list.

Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Name: FilteredList
Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Description: A new list with the elements that satisfy the condition.

ReferenceAction.Name: ListInsert
ReferenceAction.Description: Inserts an element in a specific position of a list.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: List
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The list to add the element to.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: Element
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The element to insert in the list.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: Position
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The position where the element is inserted.

ReferenceAction.Name: SetCurrentLocale
ReferenceAction.Description: Sets the language locale of the user session to change the application presentation language.

ReferenceAction.Name: Login
ReferenceAction.Description: Logs a specified user in the application. In case of success, 'UserId' and 'Username' session variables are filled with the user data.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: Persistent
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: If true, the login will be persistent for 15 days

ReferenceAction.Name: CommitTransaction
ReferenceAction.Description: Issues a database COMMIT command that makes effective all changes done on the database since the last commit.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: Tabs
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
Set of Tabs with placeholders for Title and Content.
Fill in the headers and respective content areas of the tabs to be displayed. Empty tabs will not be rendered.
Used to display large sets of information which can be split into different areas, whilst always remaining a click away.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: TabsOrientation
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the direction of the tabs. By default, the tabs are displayed horizontally.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: StartingTab
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the index of the currently active tab. The index begins at 0.
Examples: - Blank - The 1st tab is the active tab. This is the default. - 1 - The 2nd tab is the active tab.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Height
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Height of the tabs container. By default, "auto".
Examples: - Auto - The tab height adjusts to the content. This is the default. - 400px - The height of the tab is 400px.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: TabsVerticalPosition
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Sets the position of the tabs headers. By default, tabs appear on left.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: SectionIndex
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
Use the Section Index to organize a screen's content, enabling quick navigation within a page.
Just drag the pattern, and it will create a link to every section you have on the page. If you use a list of sections, add disable-virtualization=true through the Attributes section on the list widget containing the section patterns.
Use the parameter isFixed to define if it will stick on scroll and the TopPosition to change the distance to top.
Set IsSmooth to true to enable animated scroll.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: SmoothScrolling
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: If True, navigation to the destination is animated. If False, the navigation is instant. The default value is True.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: IsFixed
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: If True, the Section Index Pattern is always in the same position on the screen. This is the default. If False, the Section Index Pattern scrolls with the page content. The default value is False

Set the balloon shape. The predefined options are: - SoftRounded - Rounded - Sharp
Examples: Entities.Shape.Rounded - the inherit style will be rounded.
By default, 4px (Entities.Shape.SoftRounded).
Default: Shape.SoftRounded

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: BalloonPosition
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the balloon’s position. The predefined options are: - Auto - Top - Top start - Top end - Right - Right start - Right end - Bottom - Bottom start - Bottom end - Left - Left start - Left end
Examples: - Blank (Entities.BalloonPosition.Auto) - The placement of the balloon is automatically calculated based on the space available. This is the default. - Entities.BalloonPosition.Right - The balloon is displayed to the right of the element.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples:
Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).
"myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied.
"myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: DateFormat
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the input date format. If empty, the date format will the same as the server format. When using formats with time, make sure to set the TimeFormat property.
Here's some of the examples that you can use: • "DD/MM/YYYY" -> 23/03/2018 • "MM/DD/YYYY" -> 03/23/2018 • "DD MMM YYYY" -> 23 Mar 2018 • "DD-MMM-YYYY" -> 23-Mar-2018 • "DD.MMM.YYYY" -> 23.Mar.2018 • "MMM DDD, YYYY" -> Mar Mond, 2021 • "MMM DDD, YY" -> Mar Mond, 21 • ...

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ShowTodayButton
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to show a button below the DatePicker that allows users to pick the current day date.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: TimeFormat
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Select the format of the time (12 hours or 24 hours). By default, no time is shown (Disabled).

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: Carousel
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: Displays multiple items in a horizontal slide. Ideal for creating horizontal slides in smaller screens. For dynamic content, place a List directly inside the placeholder. Elements inside the placeholder represent different items.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Navigation
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the type of navigation of the carousel. Available options:
- Arrows: show arrows on the sides - Dots: show dots under the carousel slides - Both: show arrows and dots on the carousel - None: no navigation controls are shown

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Height
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set a custom height for the carousel. The parameter accepts any CSS format, except percentage (library constraint). By default, 'auto'.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ItemsPerSlide
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the number of items shown per slide according to the device.
- Desktop: Set the number of items that are shown simultaneously in desktop. By default, 1 item in all devices. - Tablet: Set the number of items that are shown simultaneously in tablet. By default, 1 item in all devices. - Phone: Set the number of items that are shown simultaneously in phone. By default, 1 item in all devices.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set additional parameters to customize Carousel behavior and functionality.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.Examples:
- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: OnSlideMoved
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered after the Carousel slides move.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: CarouselId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the Carousel block.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: ItemIndex
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Index of the item that is currently focused.

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: Initialized
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered after the Carousel is initialized.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: CarouselId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the Carousel block.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
Select an interval within a range of values, using two sliding handles.
For advanced options, read the official documentation: https://refreshless.com/nouislider/
Note: To ensure the correct behavior of the component, we recommend not using different versions of it in the same page.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: MaxValue

If the slider's orientation is horizontal, the size you set will be the width of the Range Slider Interval. Otherwise (vertical), the size you set will be the height. Accepts any kind of unit (px, %, vw). Default value is 100%.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set additional parameters to customize the RangeSliderInterval behavior and functionality.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.Examples:
- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered after selecting a new value on the slider. By default, the event is triggered while the user is dragging the RangeSliderInterval handler. Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: IntervalEnd

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: TimeFormat
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the input time format. If empty, the time format will be defined based on the Is24Hours parameter. Here is a list of formatting tokens that you can use:
H → Hours (24 hours) h → Hours (12 hours) G → Hours (12 hours), 2 digits with leading zeros i → Minutes s → Seconds S → Seconds, 2 digits with leading zeros K → AM/PM
You may escape formatting tokens using \\.
Examples: “H:i” → 15:30 “G:i K” → 03:30 PM ”h\\hi\\m K” → 3h30m PM ”H \\ho\\ur\\s i \\m\\i\\n\\ute\\s” → 15 hours 30 minutes

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Is24Hours
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to “True” to display the time in a 24 hour format without AM/PM selection. By default, the time is displayed using a 24 hour format.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: InitialTime
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: The initial selected time for the TimePicker. If not set, no initial time will be displayed on the input and the TimePicker will start at 12:00.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs

Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/StyleGuidePreview/Styles

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
Display an action that floats on the bottom right of the screen, providing access to a set of additional actions. Could also be placed inside a Bottom Bar.
Add the pattern to your screen. Drag as many FloatingActionsItems as you need to the Items placeholder.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: IsExpanded
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Initial state of the Block, the default value is False

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: IsHover
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to true, to use hover as interaction trigger.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.Examples:
- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Name: Items
NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Description: Drag FloatingActionItems blocks to this placeholder

NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Name: Button
NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Description: Drag the Icon widget to this placeholder.

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: OnToggle
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event fired after the floating actions are toggled

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: Video
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: Drag the pattern to the screen to add video content without the need for a third-party plug-in. Note: The URL must be a direct video file, not a website like Vimeo or YouTube since those servers provide their own embed code.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: URL
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the URL of the video file, preferably mp4 or webm format.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Controls
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set to True to sow the video controls. Set False to disable the video controls. In case of mobile, the controls will always be enable. By default, the controls are shown (True).
Default: True

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Width
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the width (in pixel or percentage) of the video. By default, the original video width is detected.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Height
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the height (in pixel or percentage) of the video. By default, the original video height is detected.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Captions
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: List of the caption tracks (language, source file and label) that will be available for the video. By default, the video has no captions.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set additional parameters to customize the Video behavior and functionality.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.Examples:
Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).
"myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied.
"myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: StateChanged
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Returns the reproduction state of the video. The different states of the video are: - Unstarted: if the video did not start being played. - Playing: if the video is being played. - Paused: if the video is currently paused. - Ended: if the video is ended.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: VideoId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the Video block.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: VideoState
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: The reproduction state of the video.

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: Initialized
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered after the Video instance is ready.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: VideoId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the Video block.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebFlow.Name: Advanced
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebFlow.Description: Flow to group patterns and components from the same category - Advanced.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: DropdownServerSide
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
Dropdown block that allows you to manage large datasets in a more flexible and efficient way. The block has less out-of-the-box logic and is targeted for more advanced use cases.
Examples: - Pagination / infinite scroll - Search based on queries - Custom dropdown balloon (with footer, buttons, title, etc.)
Check more about it in: https://success.outsystems.com/Documentation/11/Developing_an_Application/Design_UI/Patterns/Using_Mobile_and_Reactive_Patterns/Interaction/Dropdown_Server_Side

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: AllowMultipleSelection
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to allow users to select more than one option. By default, False (the dropdown only allows one option to be selected). If AllowMultipleSelection is False, the dropdown will close automatically after the user picks an option. Otherwise (if AllowMultipleSelection is True), it will remain open.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: IsDisabled
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set as True to disable the Dropdown. By default, False (the dropdown is active).

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Name: SelectedValues
NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Description: Add an Expression to show the selected option(s) value.

NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Name: BalloonSearchInput
NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Description: Add an input text. If empty this placeholder will be hidden.

NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Name: BalloonSearchInputIcon
NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Description: Add an icon. If empty, this placeholder will be hidden.

NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Name: BalloonContent
NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Description: Add a List of DropdownServerSideItem(s) in order to add options into the Dropdown.

NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Name: BalloonFooter
NRWebWidgets.ReferencePlaceholder.Description: Add the footer elements here. If empty, this placeholder will be hidden.

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: OnToggle
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered each time the DropdownServerSide opens or closes.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: DropdownServerSideId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the DropdownServerSide block.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: IsOpen
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Returns True if the DropdownServerSide was opened. False, otherwise.

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: Initialized
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered after the DropdownServerSide instance is ready.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: DropdownServerSideId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the DropdownServerSide block.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: DropdownServerSideItem
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: DropdownOptionItem block, this block should be use as a DropdownServerAction option item.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ItemId
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Identifier of the DropdownServerSide item.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: IsSelected
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to allow users to select more than one option.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: OnSelected
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered each time the item is clicked.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: DropdownId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the DropdownServerSideItem block where the clicked item is.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: DropdownItemId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the item that was clicked.

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: Initialized
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered after the DropdownServerSideItem instance is ready.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: DropdownItemId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the item that was Initialized.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: Contains the OutSystems platform licenses.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: Rating
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
Use this pattern to let your users score your products and services.
Drag the pattern to the screen and set the Rating Value parameter.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: RatingValue
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Rating number to be displayed.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: RatingScale
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Rating scale that determines the number of items to be displayed. By default, the scale is "5". If set to 1, it will behave as a 'view only' element, with IsEdit automatically set to false. The parameter maximum value is 100. If the value introduced is bigger, only 100 items will be displayed.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: IsEdit
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to allow users to interact with the pattern. Default value is False.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Size
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Sets the size of the Rating pattern. There are 3 sizes available; Small, Medium, and Base. Default size is Base.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.Examples:
- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: OnSelect
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event that returns the current rating value.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the Rating block.

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Name: Initialized
ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered after the Rating instance is ready.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: RatingId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the Rating block.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: ProgressBar
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description: You can use the ProgressBar to display the current progress in a bar.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Progress
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Progress percentage. Usually a number (integer) between 0 and 100. You can also use functions and local variables.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ProgressColor
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
The color that fills the bar, as progress goes up. By default, the progress color is the primary color you chose when creating the app.
To use an RGB color, use: TextToIdentifier(“rgb(0,0,0)“) To use an HEX color, use: TextToIdentifier(“#000000”)

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: TrailColor
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
The color of the empty part of the bar. By default, the trail color is Neutral 4 (#DEE2E6).
To use an RGB color, use: TextToIdentifier(“rgb(0,0,0)“) To use an HEX color, use: TextToIdentifier(“#000000”)

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Thickness
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Sets the height of the ProgressBar, in pixels. By default, the thickness is "12".

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Sets additional parameters to customize the ProgressBar behavior and functionality.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

ReferenceWebBlockCustomEvent.Description: Event triggered after the ProgressBar instance is ready.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: ProgressBarId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the ProgressBar block.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Progress percentage. Usually a number from from 0 to 100.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Size
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the ProgressCircle diameter (height and width). Accepts any kind of unit (px, %, vw). By default, "100%".
Example: "30%"

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: TrailColor
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
The color of the empty part of the circle. By default, the trail color is Neutral 4 (#DEE2E6).
To use an RGB color, use: TextToIdentifier(“rgb(0,0,0)“) To use an HEX color, use: TextToIdentifier(“#000000”)

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Thickness
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Sets the thickness of the circle that marks the progress, in pixels. By default, the thickness is "8".

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: OptionalConfigs
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Sets additional parameters to customize the ProgressCircle behavior and functionality.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: AccordionItem
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
An area that can be expanded or collapsed. You can change the default state of the Block using the IsExpanded input.
Can also be used within the Accordion Pattern, placed inside the Content placeholder. Drag into the Accordion Block as many items as you need.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: StartsExpanded
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Initial state of the Block. If set to True, when the page is rendered, the Accordion Item is open. If set to False, the Accordion Item is closed. The default value is False.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Icon
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the icons shown in of the AccordionItem.
You can pick between the following: - Carets - Arrow up icon when the item is expanded and arrow down icon when the item is collapsed. This is the default. - Plus/Minus - Minus icon (-) when the item is expanded and plus icon (+) when the item is collapsed. - Custom - Advanced option to customize the Accordion icons. To use custom icons, set the Icon property to Custom and drag and drop the Icon widget to the Accordion Item placeholder.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: IconPosition
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set the position of the accordion icon. By default, the icon appears on the right.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: IsDisabled
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Doesn't allow the Accordion Item to be clickable. Default value is False.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass

Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.Examples:
- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: Tooltip
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
Dynamic tooltip displaying simple content.
Drag the Block to the screen, add your content in the Content placeholder and then add the tooltip text in the Tooltip placeholder.
Use the Tooltip block to display additional information related to a screen element.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Position
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Set the Tooltip's position. Default is Right.
The predefined options are the following: - Bottom - BottomLeft - BottomRight - Center - Left - Right - Top - TopLeft - TopRight
Examples: - Entities.Position.Right - The Tooltip is displayed to the right of the element. - Entities.Position.Bottom - The Tooltip is displayed underneath the element.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: StartsOpen
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set to True to show the Tooltip when the page is first loaded (without the need for the initial trigger). If False, the tooltip is not visible. This is the default.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Trigger
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set how the tooltip is triggered. By default, the tooltip is shown on hover.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples:
- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

ReferenceClientAction.Name: CarouselEnableOnRender
ReferenceClientAction.Description:
Prevents the Carousel block from auto-updating every time that there’s a change on the Carousel items. This will prevent unnecessary destroy/init cycles of the provider, resulting in better performance.
This action can be used in combination with the CarouselDisableOnRender action (for instance, before adding a new class to an element inside the Carousel, use the CarouselDisableOnRender action and after doing it, use the CarouselEnableOnRender action, so that the carousel can auto-update if needed).
By default, the Carousel auto-updates itself.

Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Name: WidgetId
Variables.ReferenceGenericInputParameter.Description: Identifier of the Carousel block.

Variables.ReferenceGenericOutputParamete.Description: Boolean that indicates if the action was successfully performed.

NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Name: Map
NewRuntime.ReferenceWebBlock.Description:
Displays an interactive map on your Reactive Web and Native Mobile apps using the Google Maps API. You can change the default behavior of your map using all the options available in the block. Use the AddOns blocks (Markers, Shapes and DrawingTools) to customize your map. To add a list of markers, drag the List widget inside the AddOns placeholder together with the Marker.
For more information, visit https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/
Notes: - In the same application, we advise using a single map Forge component and a single Google Maps' license. - To use DrawingTools, SearchPlaces, or Directions APIs.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: APIKey
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add a Google Maps API key to display the map correctly and remove the "development purpose" watermark. There are 2 ways of setting the API key: - In the input parameter API key (in service studio or from a persistent storage) - In the site property GoogleMapsServerKey in module OutSystemsMaps
To use this feature, your API key must have Geocoding API, Maps JavaScript API and Directions API activated in the console. Keep in mind that if you have a block from OutSystemsMaps and a block from OutSystemsLocations, the API key must be the same or else an error will be returned.
You can get an API key for Google Maps here: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/get-api-key

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Center
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Defines the location of the map. Works with addresses and coordinates (latitude and longitude). If left empty, the default location is the OutSystems Boston office. Please note that the map will automatically adjust to show all markers by default. You can override this by setting Location + Zoom parameters.
On maps with markers, the default location will be the location of the first marker on the list.
GMaps - Works with addresses and coordinates (lat and lng). Example: “34.56,45.65” or “55 Thomson Pl 2nd floor, Boston, MA 02210, United States”. Leaflet - Works with coordinates (lat and lng) only. Example: “34.56,45.65”.

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: Height

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description: Set additional parameters to customize map’s behavior and functionality.

To use this feature, your API key must have Geocoding API, Maps JavaScript API and Directions API activated in the console. Keep in mind that if you have a block from OutSystemsMaps and a block from OutSystemsLocations, the API key must be the same or else an error will be returned.

ReferenceStructure.Name: OptionalStaticMapConfigs

ReferenceStructureAttribute.Description:
Sets the Zoom level to apply on map, between 1 (World) and 20 (Buildings). The following list shows the approximate level of detail you can expect to see at each zoom level: - Auto: Fit to all markers present on Map - Zoom1: World - Zoom5: Continent - Zoom10: City - Zoom15: Streets - Zoom20: Buildings
For more information, visit https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/overview#zoom-levels
ReferenceStructureAttribute.Name: Zoom

ReferenceStructureAttribute.Description:
Set the map type to roadmap, satellite, hybrid or terrain, provided by Google Maps.
For more information, visit https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/maptypes.
ReferenceStructureAttribute.Name: Type

ReferenceStructure.Description:
Use the StaticMarker parameter to set a location on the map. By default, the Marker uses the google maps defaults marker but can by displayed custom images and you can change it using the present parameters.
For more information, please visit https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/markers
ReferenceStructure.Name: StaticMarker

ReferenceStructureAttribute.Description:
Defines the marker position on the map. Works with addresses and coordinates (latitude and longitude).
Example: “34.56,45.65” or “55 Thomson Pl 2nd floor, Boston, MA 02210, United States”
ReferenceStructureAttribute.Name: Location
ReferenceStructureAttribute.Label: Location

ReferenceStructureAttribute.Description:
Set the icon image to be applied to each marker. By default, the Marker uses the Google Maps defaults marker.
Notes: - Icon images may be in PNG, JPEG or GIF formats, though PNG is recommended. - Icons may be up to 4096 pixels maximum size (64x64 for square images). - The icon image URL needs to be absolute. - Google uses cache on the custom icon images.
For more information, please visit https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/maps-static/start#CustomIcons
ReferenceStructureAttribute.Name: IconURL
ReferenceStructureAttribute.Label: Icon URL

ReferenceStructureAttribute.Description:
Allow for more options beyond what's provided through the input parameters on the marker.
To be compliant with Content Security Policy (CSP) requirements, the usage of eval() function will be discontinued. Consequently, this parameter will be impacted and may not function as expected. It's important to note that this change will only affect those who need to ensure compliance with CSP guidelines.
ReferenceStructureAttribute.Name: DEPRECATED_AdvancedFormat
ReferenceStructureAttribute.Label: DEPRECATED Advanced Format

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: EnableAccessibilityFeatures
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
When true the following Accessibility Features are enabled: - Focus States - Skip To Content - Accessible Links - Enhanced Contrasts
These features are implemented in CSS using the "has-accessible-features" Selector

Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Name: ExtendedClass
Variables.ReferenceSerializableInputPara.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.
Examples: - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value). - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied. - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.
You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/ResourcesPage
